newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Charts, sentiment sour in precious metal.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Charts, sentiment sour in precious metal.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
-----------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - April 23-------------
Gold prices may turn lower to test nearby support at $340 in the near term after failing to break out of range to the upside, traders and analysts said.
Silver also may have downside probes on the horizon, while platinum shows the most upside potential, they added.
GOLD - Upside impetus was still lacking from the range-trading, relatively quiet market, and prices may turn down in the near term, dealers said.
A breach of $340 support would target last week's low of $337.50 and then the February 12 low of $336.15, chartists said.
Analysts have said gold needed to break above $345 resistance very soon in order to reduce downside pressure.
"Sentiment has changed as of today, especially with the dollar rising. People are a bit more bearish," a European bullion dealer said.

He noted that the market had registered no reaction on Wednesday morning to a Bundesbank statement reiterating its opposition to Internationl Monetary Fund gold sales, saying these could hurt the IMF's credibility.
"OK, they've said it before, but it should still be bullish for gold," a dealer said. "But so far it's had no effect."
The dealer added that that market was quiet and he saw no evidence so far of producer selling or rumoured central bank selling.
The Dutch central bank said it was not currently selling gold from its reserves following talk in New York that an unnamed European central bank was selling reserves.
At 0745 GMT spot gold was indicated at $340.55/$341.05 per ounce, down $0.55 from Tuesday's New York close.
SILVER - Prices needed to breach $4.85 resistance or risk heading lower, dealers said. On the downside $4.60-$4.65 was important support.
Silver's 10-day moving average was stalled at $4.75, and dealers said they suspected the next move from that plateau might be lower rather than higher.
"A bearish outside day (on Tuesday) is suggestive of further weakness, as we look for futher tests of initial support at $4.65," brokers Rudolf Wolff said in a report.
At 0745 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.72/$4.74 an ounce, down one cent from Tuesday's New York close.
PLATINUM - Platinum prices were consolidating around $375, some $5 down from Tuesday morning levels. But a bounce to $385 resistance was still very possible in the near term, technical analysts said.
A near-convergence of 10- and 30-day moving averages on Wednesday morning at just above $372 an ounce would provide support there, they added.
At 0745 GMT spot platinum was indicated at $375.00/$376.00 per ounce, down $1.50 from Tuesday's New York close.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
